extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, researchers, and readers interested in news transparency
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and indicators developed by The Trust Project to increase transparency and accountability in news reporting, including metadata/markup, editorial policies, and disclosures about authorship, methodology, corrections, and conflicts. Intended to guide newsrooms and signal reliability to platforms and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Trust Indicators and editorial attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The consortium has created a standardized content management system (CMS), editorial guidelines, and style guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reflect the consortium's shared principles through policies on ethics, corrections, anonymous sourcing, and fact-checking standards; implemented as part of site UX and metadata to surface information about reporting and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of markup language / metadata (trust indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: News articles use markup language, user experience (UX) as 'pieces of online code to deliver improved search and news results' by providing readers with information including the author/journalist and how the story was reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust indicators are encoded in CMS/markup so platforms and search engines can surface reliability signals; examples include metadata fields for author, reporting details, and other disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of the author/journalist and how the story was reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing readers with information including the author/journalist and how the story was reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary indicator to help readers assess who produced the story and what reporting steps were taken; typically surfaced via bylines, author bios, and reporting-method notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in the reporting process and editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Project looks for transparency in the reporting process, including explaining some editorial decisions for major stories, being easier for readers to contact and making other disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explanatory notes on editorial choices, contact information for reporters/editors, and other disclosures that clarify how coverage was produced and why decisions were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies on ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium members adopt policies on ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the shared editorial attributes; ethical policies should be articulated and accessible so readers can evaluate newsroom standards and norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy and visible corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards include corrections (the use of corrections with links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should publish corrections with links and make correction practices transparent so readers can see how errors are handled and learn what changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous sourcing policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies addressing anonymous sourcing are part of the Trust Project standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should explain when anonymous sources are used, why, and how reliability is assessed; policies should be visible to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The consortium's shared principles include fact-checking standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should document fact-checking practices and standards used to verify claims and sources, enabling readers to assess rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of methodology (who was interviewed, what was researched)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early ideas included disclosure of their methodology including 'whom they interviewed' and 'what they researched'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology disclosures make reporting transparent by listing research steps, sources consulted, and other investigative methods used for the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full disclosure of contributors to an article
rubrics_metrics.description: Full disclosure of all contributors to the content of an article including researchers, editors, and lawyers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution should extend beyond the byline to include researchers, editors, legal reviewers, and other contributors so readers understand who influenced the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist background and conflict disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure by journalists of their background regarding level of expertise and 'areas of personal interest and conflict'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author bios or disclosures should include relevant expertise and potential conflicts of interest to help readers evaluate perspective and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-focused certification rather than public scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The project does not report on outlets that did not pass or share the final score of those that did, just the process it takes to pass and the standards that must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes documenting and publishing the standards and steps for certification rather than publishing numeric scores or pass/fail lists; focuses on transparency of process.
